outcomes: In a Dart or Flutter repository, each Dart package is a component, named by its directory and its pubspec name, without a Putnami file
A path dependency, and inside a pub workspace or a melos repository a dependency on another of its packages, is an edge, so a change to a shared package marks the apps that use it as dependent
The coverage/lcov.info that flutter test --coverage writes in each package and the JUnit report tojunit writes land on the right package, and a pubspec.lock bump is a dependency change
nonGoals: Running dart, flutter, pub or melos, or reading the pub cache, .dart_tool or pubspec_overrides.yaml
Computing the changed and dependent components, the tests and coverage per component, the changed-line coverage and the lockfile diff: the change analyses own them
The native iOS and Android projects of a Flutter app, which the Swift and Gradle detectors read
Serving the detector over the workspace probe wire or from its own extension: it lives in @putnami/observe

requirements.text: Past build, node_modules, Pods and hidden directories, each directory whose pubspec.yaml names a package is a component of ecosystem dart, named by its pubspec name. A member of the root pubspec.yaml workspace list, and a directory the root melos.yaml packages globs match less its ignore globs, are of source workspace; any other is of source manifest. A root pubspec.yaml that declares a workspace or sits beside melos.yaml is no component. A pubspec.yaml or melos.yaml that does not read is a diagnostic.

A component depends on another when an entry of its dependencies, dev_dependencies or dependency_overrides gives a path that resolves to the other's directory, or, inside a pub workspace or a melos repository, when the entry names the other's package with no source of its own. A git, sdk or hosted source, a path outside the repository or to no component, and the component itself are no edge.

pubspec.lock is a lockfile of ecosystem pub: each entry of its packages gives its name and version, and an entry of source path or sdk is the repository's own code or the SDK's and is no dependency. A lockfile that does not read is the observe.lockfile_unreadable warning. In a pub workspace the root pubspec.lock pins the packages of every member; it lies in no component, and its change names none.

The paths of an LCOV report under a package, such as the coverage/lcov.info flutter test --coverage writes, read first from that package's directory. A JUnit case of a tojunit report, whose class name is its test file's path without _test.dart with each / written as a ., goes to the package that holds that file, else to the package that holds the report.

On a melos repository with apps/mobile, a Flutter app that depends on packages/pricing through a path, and packages/ui, where a change edits pricing and bumps a package in pubspec.lock, the analyses list the three packages with the edge to pricing, mark mobile dependent and ui unaffected; the coverage/lcov.info of each package and the tojunit report land on the packages, with no unattributed case and no unmapped file; and the bump is a pub dependency change.
